page.layout: One printed page, one text column with a narrow right margin holding side notes. Running head at top. No page number printed. The numbered theses 10 to 19 run down the column, with the notes beside them in the right margin.

main_text.p: De fœde-ribus.10. Fœdera licita sunt quidem ahenea: sed iis confi-dere valde lubricum est.
Fœderum infelicitatis causæ hic enodantur: quæ sunt,
De muni-tionibus.11. In munitionibus vana hominum fiducia.
De hostium diffidiis alendis.12. Discordias inter hostes serere, magna quidem est prudentiæ & utilitatis: verùm civitatem aliquam diffidiis intestinis laborantem invade-re, non caret periculo.
constantiâ:13. Civitati liberæ bellum inferre, arduum nimis & periculosum.
contumelia:14. Conviciis hostem ad vindictam inflammare, stultum.
contemptu:15. Hostem præ nimiâ victoriæ confidentiâ contemnere, stultum.
De insidiis17. Insidia in hostes licita. Docetur hic,
main_text.l: Insidiæ in hostes quare sint licitæ?
main_text.p: In insidiis hosti struendis cavendam esse perfidiam: utpote quæ perfidis ipsis est perniciosa.
De despera-to hoste~:18. Bella cum desperatis plerumq; sunt infelicia.
De potentis hostis tra-ctatione~19. Hostes potentes aut necandi, aut maximis beneficiis sunt obligandi.

page.notes: The tilde-like hook after some side notes ("provocatione", "hoste", "tractatione") is a printed ligature or hook sign; it is copied as "~" and is not a letter. The word "ahenea" is read as printed. No page number is printed. The running head is the only head at the top. Long s is transcribed as s throughout.
